correctness.rationale: A strict majority tie-retaining symmetric-graph Lyapunov function proves eventual period at most two. When hub fixed zero, four fixed local triples (000,011,110,111) give (1+z)^2 adjacent one-count per blade; complement symmetry yields E_k=4^k+binom(2k,k). On a nonfixed two-cycle the hub must flip: if fixed, leaf endpoints evolve monotonically. The exhaustive eight-triple local two-step table leaves (000↔000),(101↔010),(111↔111), with counts a,b,c; hub flips precisely when 2c<k<2(b+c). Thus Q_k is exactly the multinomial count, and multinomial concentration proves Q_k/3^k→1 and recurrent 2-cycle-state fraction ∼2(3/4)^k. Independent exhaustive direct state evaluation matched E,Q for k=1..5: (6,1),(22,1),(84,13),(326,21),(1276,141); finite checks corroborate the all-k proof.

evidence: General eventual period at most two is classical and dominates only the possible period lengths, not the number of recurrent states on a specified graph.
